summary: Dependency-free CSV parse and write that handles quoted fields correctly.
overview: Reads and writes the CSV dialect Excel and Google Sheets use natively, so a spreadsheet is a practical data pipeline into Unity with no .xlsx library involved. It handles the part a naive string.Split(',') gets wrong: commas and newlines inside quoted fields, and a doubled "" meaning a literal quote.
useCases: Authoring item, enemy or dialogue tables in a spreadsheet and reading them at runtime or import time.
Exporting captured play data for analysis in a spreadsheet.
Round-tripping data through the CSV Table Editor window without a binary format.

gotchas.title: Rows are string arrays, not typed objects
gotchas.body: Parse returns List<string[]> with no header handling and no type conversion. Deciding row 0 is a header, and turning "12" into an int, is the caller's job.

gotchas.title: Ragged rows are preserved, not padded
gotchas.body: A row with fewer fields than the header comes back shorter. Index defensively, or normalise after parsing.
